clue.text: Unwilling to move fortune into busted flush

indicators.note: the word for fortune is placed inside the rearranged letters
something busted is broken apart, so the letters of the word flush are rearranged

parts.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A poker player whose winning flush went bust is too dispirited to budge from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' and 'busted' both sound like poker, which hides that 'busted' is the anagram signal and 'into' the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lazy and idle is reluctant to stir, the very picture of a person who will not move.

clue.text: Note informant among 52 scholarly people

indicators.note: the note and the informant sit among the letters standing for the number

parts.note: 52 in Roman numerals is LII
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a rat is slang for someone who informs on others

explanation.surface: A note from a police informer is passed around among a group of educated people.
explanation.walkthrough: A number in a clue often stands for its Roman numerals; 'among' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the collective name for well-read, learned people, the intelligentsia of letters.

clue.text: Backed-up transport to make sound of airways

indicators.note: in a down clue backed up means read from the bottom upwards, reversing the transport word

parts.note: a cart is a simple means of transport
to heal is to make well, sound again

explanation.surface: Reversing a vehicle seems to be offered as a way to cure breathing problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed-up' suits a down clue, read upwards; 'sound' looks like noise but means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the main airway, and this adjective describes things relating to that tube.

clue.text: Square vaguely remembered losing a grand

indicators.note: losing tells us to drop the thousand from the word for hazily recalled

parts.note: a foggy memory is a vague, hazy one
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone only hazily recalls losing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes one G from FOGGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Square in its slang sense means old-fashioned and conventional, which is exactly what a fusty old person is.

clue.text: Failed to take away the air of disappointment

definitions.meaning: to have failed someone is to have disappointed them, a verb sense
to deflate a tyre or balloon by releasing its air
an anticlimax or let-off of expectations, a noun sense

explanation.surface: A deflating moment is described as failing to clear the air of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions joined by the link words 'to' and 'of'; the past-tense verb, the deflation and the noun all share the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Each part names one sense: failing someone, deflating a tyre, and an anticlimax.

clue.text: Barnsley's wingers splitting team twice in a row

indicators.note: the pair of wing letters goes between the two copies of the team, splitting them
twice tells us the team word is used two times

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
the outer letters of Barnsley are B and Y

explanation.surface: Barnsley's wide players are breaking up the opposition twice in a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnsley is a Yorkshire town with a football club, so 'wingers' looks like football; it means the word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed next to each other, adjacent, form a line or row.

clue.text: Where to arrange flowers around climber almost like Japanese knotweed?

indicators.note: the flower-holder phrase goes around the shortened climbing plant

parts.note: flowers are arranged in a vase

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the plant is dropped

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether to put ivy in a flower arrangement, though it spreads like knotweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Japanese knotweed is a notoriously aggressive weed in Britain that damages buildings; 'almost' cuts IVY to IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotweed is the classic example of an aggressive non-native plant that spreads uncontrollably.

clue.text: Mimic runs performing group with no name

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: with no tells us to remove the name letter from the group

parts.note: an ensemble is a group of musicians or actors

explanation.surface: An impressionist does a sketch running through a nameless band's act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' is the deletion signal; R for runs comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic something is to look or sound like it, to be similar to it.

clue.text: Rising ground enclosed in English pit

indicators.note: the short form of enclosed is put in the English pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit, as in a coal pit
enc. is the standard abbreviation for enclosed, as on a letter

explanation.surface: A hill or mound has been fenced inside an English colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ENC inside MINE after E. ENC is the abbreviation for 'enclosed' that you see at the foot of a business letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of high, elevated land such as a hill or knoll is an old word sense of eminence.

clue.text: Craft reversing into view without turning

indicators.note: into places the backwards craft word inside the view word

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: reversing means the word for craft is read backwards

parts.note: art is a craft or skill

explanation.surface: A boat is reversed into sight without any turn being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat, which suits 'reversing', but it means skill; 'into' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or line that never bends goes direct, with no curves at all.

clue.text: Say equine group with no leader goes over Lipizzaner's performance?

indicators.note: goes over signals that the whole string is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
an ass is an equine animal

indicators.note: with no leader removes the first letter of the group word

parts.note: a herd is a group of animals

explanation.surface: A herd of horses without its lead animal crosses over for a show by Vienna's famous white horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no leader' cuts HERD to ERD; 'goes over' reverses EG+ASS+ERD. Lipizzaners are the white horses of Vienna's Spanish Riding School.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipizzaners are famed for intricate trained horse movements, the art of equestrian display.

clue.text: After triumph in vote, a means to escape

indicators.note: After places the phrase for a means following the phrase for winning a vote

parts.note: the ayes have it is how a winning vote in Parliament is announced
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: After winning an election, a politician looks for a getaway route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ayes have it' is the Speaker's formula declaring a vote won in the House of Commons. The phrase is British slang for to escape or abscond.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang phrase means to make off or abscond, to get away.

clue.text: Prepare to do battle with a rump steak somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unexpected arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner gears up for a fight with a tough cut of beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges A RUMP STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: To get ready for war is to take weapons in hand, an idiom for going to fight.

clue.text: The writer's accepted by Pound as a member

indicators.note: accepted by means the writer's contraction is taken inside the pound symbol

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
the writer is I, so the writer's is I'm

explanation.surface: A writer is admitted as a member of Ezra Pound's circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, a crossword convention; 'accepted by' signals insertion, and 'as a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is one of the body's members, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Ultimately, hatred favours hostility

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of hatred

parts.note: to favour a parent is to take after them, to be like them

explanation.surface: In the end, hatred is said to breed animosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favours' here means resembles, as a child favours a parent, giving IS LIKE after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility and aversion are close synonyms for a feeling of antipathy towards something.

clue.text: Swallow to flap without gusto?

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it
birds beat their wings, flap them

explanation.surface: A swallow flaps its wings in a half-hearted way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, which suits 'flap', but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something muted and gloomy lacks zest and enthusiasm; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Flight of fancy was arty ingénue's debut

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged
debut points to the first letter of the young actress word

explanation.surface: An innocent young actress, trying to look artistic at her first appearance, indulges in a flight of fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight of fancy' looks like one phrase but 'Flight' is the definition and 'fancy' the anagram signal on WAS ARTY plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a set of steps between floors.

clue.text: Fuel being short hampers officer commanding bishop's area

indicators.note: the shortened fuel word encloses the officer, hampering him
being short means the fuel word loses its last letter

parts.note: diesel is a fuel
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: A fuel shortage hinders an army commander working in a church district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being short' signals dropping the last letter; 'hampers' signals that the fuel word holds the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the district a bishop oversees, an ecclesiastical see.

clue.text: Blue note in middle of Alcina? Don't talk like a fool

indicators.note: the sad note goes into the centre letters of the opera name
middle of picks the central pair of letters of Alcina

parts.note: blue means sad, low
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: An audience member is hushed for chatting through a sad aria in Handel's opera Alcina.
explanation.walkthrough: Alcina is a Handel opera, so 'Blue note' reads as music; 'middle of' and 'in' are the selection and insertion signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting the buffoon or clown is silly, foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Writ in inferior American-Gothic style? Not for Scots

parts.note: sub means below or inferior, as in substandard
Edgar Allan Poe was the master of American Gothic fiction
na is Scots for not

explanation.surface: A legal document is written in second-rate horror prose, and the Scots object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American-Gothic' suggests Grant Wood's painting, but it means the style of Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal writ ordering someone to attend court is the classic example of such an order.

clue.text: There's nothing that's disgusting about mounting support for shortest book

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the upturned support

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of disgust

indicators.note: mounting means going upwards, so in a down clue the support word is read backwards

parts.note: aid is support or help

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at nothing in particular while climbing on a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reads upwards in a down clue; 'about' signals the exclamation wrapping around; 'There's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: This prophet's book has only twenty-one verses, the briefest in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Possible report of banger with cured meat

parts.note: ham is meat cured by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: A sausage is served alongside some smoked meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang for a sausage, which suits the meat, but here it is a firework; its report is its bang.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploding firework makes a loud noise, which a comic-strip sound word could represent.

clue.text: Sumerian city recitation, recalled in over half of Bible, one addressed as a blessing

parts.note: Ur was a city of ancient Sumer

indicators.note: the backwards recitation word goes inside the start of the scripture
over half of takes the first three of the five letters of Bible
recalled means called back, so the recitation word is read backwards

parts.note: learning by rote is learning by repetition, recitation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An ancient city's chant is partly recited back from scripture as a benediction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses, 'in' inserts, and 'over half of' takes three of five letters; 'addressed as' links. The papal blessing is addressed to Rome and the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names the Pope's solemn benediction given to the city of Rome and the whole world.

clue.text: Heart surgeon tours unknown beastly place

indicators.note: the surgeon's name goes around the unknown, touring it

parts.note: Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A cardiac surgeon travels around some unknown, awful location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' suggests horrid, but here means full of beasts, farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard is a place full of livestock, so it is literally a beastly spot.

clue.text: Belly accommodating large surfeit

indicators.note: accommodating means the belly word holds the large letter within it

parts.note: gut means belly

explanation.surface: A big stomach holds an excess of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts L inside GUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversupply or excess of something is a surplus, the same idea as a surfeit.

clue.text: Limited changes involving Liberal — not right now?

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters wrap around the Liberal letter
changes signals that the letters of limited are altered in order

explanation.surface: A limited set of political changes involving the Liberals is mistimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns LIMITED into ILTIMED; 'involving' puts L inside after IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inopportune or badly timed comes at the wrong moment, not the right one.

clue.text: An accountant trained to overturn world of study

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: to overturn means the trained word is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it, so trained is aimed

explanation.surface: An accountant is coached to upset the world of learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' reverses AIMED to DEMIA. CA, chartered accountant, is a British qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: The universities and scholars together form the scholarly community and environment.

clue.text: Playwright's wife leaving area admits clubs hold opening

indicators.note: admits means the shortened name takes the clubs letter inside
leaving means the area letter departs from the wife's name

parts.note: Anne Hathaway was Shakespeare's wife
C is short for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife leaves a space, letting in some card clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops the second A of the surname; 'admits' signals insertion; C for clubs comes from card games.
explanation.definitionFit: The hold of a ship is reached through a deck opening with a hatch cover.
